questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.explanation: You should downshift before entering a curve. This helps you control the vehicle better.

questions.question: What should you do if a passenger is drunk?

options.text: Stop immediately and ask them to exit the bus.
Wait until a safe area, like a scheduled stop, and ask them to exit the bus.
Give them coffee to help them sober up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until a safe area, like a scheduled stop, and ask them to exit the bus.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for the safety of all passengers. If a passenger is drunk, wait for a safe place to let them exit. This could be the next scheduled stop or a well-lit area with other people nearby.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Only if you think there is a problem.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you see traffic and spot problems with your own vehicle.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, how many points of contact must you keep with the vehicle?
questions.explanation: When exiting, face the vehicle and always keep three points of contact. If driving a bus, hold the handrail. Not following this rule can result in automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire fails?

options.text: Keep one hand on the wheel and wave to other drivers with your other hand.

questions.explanation: Using brakes when a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Unless you must brake to avoid danger, stay off the brakes until the vehicle slows down. Then brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.

questions.question: When you start the engine, what should happen to the warning lights and buzzers?

options.text: They turn on and stay on.

questions.explanation: After starting the engine, all warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away. These include lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a concern when checking tires?

options.text: Using radial and bias-ply tires together
Rear tires with at least 2/32 inch of tread

questions.correctAnswerText: Rear tires with at least 2/32 inch of tread
questions.explanation: Check that air pressure is correct, front tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread, and rear tires have at least 2/32 inch of tread. Never mix radial and bias-ply tires together. Having the required tread depth is acceptable and not a cause for concern.

questions.question: What should you do with a retarder in icy conditions?

options.text: Use it only on the rear wheels.

questions.explanation: Turn off the retarder on icy roads. Using it when traction is poor can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: What should you do when asked to change lanes during the skills test?

options.text: Check traffic first before changing lanes.
Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow instructions.
Do not change lanes if you do not want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic first before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: During the driving skills test, you will make several lane changes. Always check traffic first and use your signals. Change lanes smoothly only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you check before driving in winter?
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check your heating and defrosting equipment, coolant and antifreeze levels, wipers and washers, tire tread, tire chains, lights, reflectors, and exhaust system. Clear all ice and snow from windows, mirrors, handholds, steps, and the radiator. Make sure the winterfront is not too tight.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the steering box is firmly attached.
Check that the steering box has no leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are there.
questions.explanation: Before driving, make sure the steering box is securely fastened. Check for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Also check for power steering fluid leaks and damage to hoses.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Never be done the same way twice in a row.
Always be done in the same order.
Only be done when it is sunny.
Not be done if you think the vehicle is working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you do not miss anything.

questions.question: Why should your mirrors show the road behind you and part of your vehicle?

options.text: Seeing only the road would make the driver feel sick.
Seeing part of the truck helps you judge distances to other vehicles.
It is against the law to show only the road.
You need to see reflections of vehicles on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing part of the truck helps you judge distances to other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle should be visible in your mirrors. This gives you a reference point to judge how close other drivers and objects are to you.

questions.question: If the driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not need to do anything about crossings.
May need to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, if your route does not have a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain or show how you would cross railroad tracks at a pretend location.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, how far behind the vehicle ahead should you stay?
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, leave one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.

questions.question: When driving a bus with passengers, you should:

options.text: Fuel the bus while passengers are on board.

questions.explanation: Do not talk with passengers to avoid distraction. Do not fuel a bus with passengers inside. Do not tow or push a broken bus with passengers aboard unless it is unsafe for them to leave the bus.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you will lose points if you:
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each time this happens, you lose points.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a long downhill slope, you should:

options.text: Turn the engine off and back on to fix the brakes.
Look for an escape ramp or other way to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for an escape ramp or other way to stop.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, use an escape ramp if available. If not, look for another escape route, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: Rims that have been welded:

options.text: Are okay to use on the rear tires.
Are okay to use when carrying heavy loads.
Are okay to use on combination vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check your wheels before driving, looking for damage to wheels and rims. Wheels or rims with welding repairs are unsafe and should not be used.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to see you and move out of your way or warn you. Always signal before changing lanes.
